extracted.intended_audience: researchers and OSF users who register or preregister systematic reviews; open science community members
extracted.subtask_description: Using a generalized, discipline-agnostic OSF registration template to preregister and archive systematic review study designs, data, and analysis code so they are persistent, discoverable, and aligned with reporting standards. The page describes template design goals, alignment with guidelines, and community-driven refinement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment with established reporting guidelines (e.g., PRISMA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure the template aligns with well established reporting guidelines (e.g., PRISMA) so that researchers can continue to abide by the rigorous standards of their communities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The template was refined to reflect recent guideline changes and to align with established community reporting standards; users should map their registration responses to relevant reporting checklists such as PRISMA to maintain community-accepted rigor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preregistration / accurate and comprehensive pre-data documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Place open science best practices at the forefront by focusing on accurate and comprehensive documentation before data was collected (i.e., preregistration).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registration refers to archiving one’s study design and outputs (e.g., data or analysis code) so that this information is immutable and persistently available in a public repository; preregistration should capture study design, planned analyses, and intended outputs prior to data collection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discipline-agnostic (generalizability across disciplines)
rubrics_metrics.description: Create a discipline-agnostic template to fit the need for registration of systematic reviews across different fields.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The template was developed and iteratively refined with community input to improve its generalizability across disciplines while remaining usable for domain-specific practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improve rigor and credibility by prompting detailed study planning
rubrics_metrics.description: Focus on improving rigor and credibility by challenging research teams to think through study details.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The template is designed to prompt detailed planning (e.g., inclusion/exclusion criteria, search strategies, analysis plans) so teams consider and document methodological choices that affect review quality and credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Usability and fit with OSF infrastructure
rubrics_metrics.description: Adjust template questions so they fit with how they would be presented on OSF Registries and align with OSF infrastructure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refinements included changing wording and presentation to match OSF's registration UI; templates should be practical for users to complete within the registry interface.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reflect recent developments and guideline changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Refine the template to reflect recent developments in the scientific community and align it with updated guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Templates should be periodically updated to incorporate evolving best practices, newly released reporting guidelines, or community-driven changes to ensure continued relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Archive study design and outputs (immutability and persistent availability)
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrations should archive study design and outputs (e.g., data or analysis code) so that information is immutable and persistently available in a public repository.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage linking or depositing data, analysis code, and other outputs in the registration to enable transparency and reproducibility; use OSF Registries or indexed community registries to ensure persistence and discoverability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community development and expert feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop and refine the template with community creators and experts via calls and feedback to improve generalizability and usability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conduct community consultations, solicit expert input, and iterate based on feedback to ensure the template meets diverse needs and remains user-friendly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address critical gaps not covered by other templates
rubrics_metrics.description: Fill critical gaps that templates in other registries did not address for systematic review registrations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify where existing templates (e.g., secondary or qualitative analysis templates) fall short for systematic reviews and include specific items/questions to cover those unmet needs, producing a more comprehensive registration form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public availability and shareability of the template
rubrics_metrics.description: Make the finalized template publicly available on OSF for all users to create registrations or download a copy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the template is openly accessible (downloadable and usable) so researchers across disciplines can adopt it for transparent preregistration of systematic reviews.
